name: external-stack-opt-in-test
status: Controller G8 run 7e74b8359bcd and G9 run 68a6f0745be1 passed with real Gateway, User, isolated MySQL and approved Redis identities. G9 produced two real v2 logout events, exercised test-consumer crash and recovery and verified Jaeger parent linkage and User resource attributes; see reports/microservices/g9-real-observed-68a6f0745be1/result.json. Real Agent and business consumers were not validated.
execution: Build the user JAR first. From knode-user run Maven test with -Dtest=ExternalStackIT -Dknode.it.real.enabled=true -Dknode.it.gateway.jar=<absolute-built-gateway-jar>; invoke Maven through Python. Never place credentials in Maven arguments.
safety_guards: JDBC URL must be jdbc:mysql://127.0.0.1:<explicit non-3306 port>/<schema> with no query, and the schema must initially contain no tables.
All three Redis identities are explicitly supplied through environment variables. No account creation or ACL mutation is performed.
Only this run's random test keys and newly created session IDs are touched. No SCAN, KEYS, old business keys, other processes, or real credentials.
Subprocess stdout and stderr are discarded to avoid credential, token, or key disclosure; exact process handles are stopped.

acl_handshake.note: Review and provision dedicated accounts separately. The test itself never executes ACL SETUSER, ACL DELUSER, or inspects existing ACLs. Handshake commands below are the exact synthetic operations; placeholders are substituted locally, and secrets must not appear in command lines or logs.
write_identity: For each newly issued test session: SET <auth-prefix><sid> <session> NX PX <ttl>; DEL <auth-prefix><sid>
acl_handshake.client_handshake: The Redis client may also issue HELLO, CLIENT SETINFO and connection setup commands depending on server and driver version; verify necessary connection commands separately without widening key access.

limitations: This file is an opt-in test specification; the controller reports are evidence for the specific G8 and G9 runs, not all versions or environments.
The G8 and G9 reports cover only the approved stack and temporary ACLs used in those runs; other TLS configurations and real Agent/business consumer integration remain pending.
Only locally built User and controller-provided Gateway JARs are launched.
